scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #5091: PC1 (10.1.0.100) and the other VLAN 10 hosts in Office A report
their default gateway (10.1.0.1) is intermittently unreachable -- it eventually
responds but latency is high. VLAN 40 (Laptop1) and VLAN 99 are unaffected.
The on-site tech swapped the patch cable and is now convinced the access switch
aswa2 has failed and is dropping frames intermittently; they want approval to
replace aswa2. Please confirm the aswa2 hardware failure and identify the port.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-dswa1-vlan10-svi-down: the VLAN 10 SVI
(br10, 10.1.0.2/24) on dswa1 is administratively down. dswa1 is the VRRP MASTER
for the VLAN 10 VIP 10.1.0.1 (priority 105); when its br10 SVI goes down,
keepalived on dswa1 stops sending VRRP advertisements and dswa2 (BACKUP,
priority 1) eventually takes over the VIP. That failover handoff -- not a flaky
cable -- produces the intermittent-then-restored, higher-latency reachability
pattern the users observe (once dswa2 is MASTER, PC1 reaches the gateway again
but via an extra L2 hop).

The TWIST: the ticket blames aswa2 and asks to replace it. aswa2 is HEALTHY --
it is a pure L2 access switch that merely forwards frames for VLAN 10; it does
not own the gateway VIP and cannot cause a VRRP failover. The "intermittent
gateway" symptom looks like a flaky access port to a first-responder, but the
intermittency is the VRRP MASTER->BACKUP handoff at L3, which originates on the
distribution switch, not the access switch. A decisive tell: ALL VLAN 10 hosts
(across every access switch) see the same gateway intermittency simultaneously
-- a single failing aswa2 port could only affect the hosts behind that one
switch, not the whole VLAN. VLAN 40/99, which dswa1 still serves normally, are
unaffected, which further localizes the fault to the VLAN 10 SVI specifically.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = dswa1 (VLAN 10 SVI / br10
down). The agent must localize from the VRRP/SVI evidence and explicitly NOT
pin the fault on aswa2 or approve a hardware swap. An agent that "confirms the
aswa2 failure" has followed the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix:
`ip link set br10 up` on dswa1.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1
scoring_axes: must-identify-svi-gateway-down: VLAN 10 SVI / br10 down causing VRRP MASTER->BACKUP failover
bonus-exonerates-aswa2: notes aswa2 is a healthy L2 access switch and does not own the gateway VIP

line.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on dswa1: its VLAN 10 SVI (`br0.10`) has been administratively
brought DOWN post-startup. The device's own startup script explicitly executes
`ip link set br0.10 up`, yet `ip link show br0.10` confirms the interface is
currently in state DOWN with no UP/LOWER_UP flags. Every other SVI on dswa1
(br0.20, br0.40, br0.99) is UP and healthy — the suppression is specific to
VLAN 10.

dswa1 is the VRRP MASTER (priority 105, virtual_router_id 10) for the VLAN 10
gateway VIP 10.1.0.1, bound to interface br0.10. With br0.10 down, dswa1 could
not send VRRP advertisements. dswa2 (BACKUP, priority 1) timed out waiting for
those advertisements and promoted itself to MASTER, acquiring 10.1.0.1/32 on
its own br0.10 — confirmed live on dswa2. Both keepalived processes have since
exited, leaving the VIP stranded on dswa2.

The intermittent high-latency symptom arises because all VLAN 10 traffic from
PC1 now takes an indirect L2 path: aswa2 → dswa1 (STP forwarding port, since
dswa1 is the STP root with bridge priority 4096) → dswa1's bridge peer link
(bond0) → dswa2, which holds the only active gateway. The direct path
aswa2.eth2 → dswa2 is STP-blocked. During the VRRP failover dead-interval
(advert_int 4 s × ~3 = ~12 s), the VIP was absent entirely — explaining the
"intermittent unreachability" phase. VLANs 40 and 99 are unaffected because
dswa1's br0.40 and br0.99 remain UP.

aswa2 is fully healthy: no interface errors, correct VLAN membership, and
normal STP port states. The on-site tech's hardware-failure hypothesis is
incorrect.

Root cause: dswa1's VLAN 10 SVI (br0.10) was administratively shut down,
collapsing the VRRP MASTER role and eliminating the direct L3 gateway for all
Office-A VLAN 10 hosts.

Corrective fix: On dswa1, run `ip link set br0.10 up` to restore the SVI, then
`systemctl start keepalived` on both dswa1 and dswa2 so dswa1 re-wins the VRRP
election (priority 105 beats dswa2's priority 1) and reclaims 10.1.0.1 as
MASTER, restoring optimal forwarding.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-svi-gateway-down: VLAN 10 SVI / br10 down causing VRRP MASTER->BACKUP failover
per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies dswa1's VLAN 10 SVI (br0.10) as administratively down, causing the VRRP MASTER→BACKUP failover rather than a failure of aswa2.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-aswa2: notes aswa2 is a healthy L2 access switch and does not own the gateway VIP
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states aswa2 is healthy (no interface errors, correct VLANs, normal STP) and clarifies the gateway VIP is owned by the distribution devices (dswa1/dswa2), exonerating aswa2.
It directs bringing the VLAN 10 SVI back up on dswa1 (ip link set br0.10 up) and restarting keepalived so dswa1 reclaims the VRRP VIP, which will restore correct operation.

Investigation log shows dswa1's br0.10 is DOWN while dswa2's br0.10 is UP and the agent validated keepalived/VRRP roles and aswa2 port health; the conclusions follow logically though a few specific assertions (exact priority numbers, STP block location, 'all hosts' observation) are only partially evidenced in the log.
